messages:
Carlos (Eng): Quick question - moving to Tijuana next month and planning to cross into San Diego for office days most weekdays. Start date 2026-10-04. 1) Do I still get WFH stipend for days I'm remote from Tijuana? 2) Any payroll/state/cross-border withholding or nexus implications? 3) Are there any border/immigration paperwork the company needs to know about for equipment shipping?
Nina (People Ops): Thanks for flagging, Carlos. Short answers: stipend can be prorated for days you work remotely from outside the US, but cross-border commuting has extra checks. Please fill the relocate/travel form and choose "cross-border commuter" so we log dates and frequency: https://redwood.internal/relocate-form.
Ravi (Payroll): Important: if you live in MX but work physically in the US on most weekdays, payroll withholding and tax residency get complicated. We'll need to know whether you will be paid as US employee (W-2) or if you'll be switching to a local MX payroll/contractor arrangement. For daily commuters we often keep US payroll but we must record days worked in each country. Fill the form and we'll run a payroll vendor review.
Diego (Legal): Cross-border commuting raises immigration and labor law considerations. If you're entering the US on a B1/B2 or border permit, that's personal; company shouldn't direct immigration behavior. On the company side, Legal needs to track if employees are habitually working from outside the US — that can affect local labor laws and PE risk. Please add an activity note on the form: expected days/week in US vs MX and whether you'll meet any local clients.
Carlos (Eng): I'll be physically in SD office Mon-Fri mornings and back in Tijuana afternoons (most days). No local clients in MX, just offices in SD. I plan to keep Redwood health benefits as-is.
Ravi (Payroll): Okay that pattern (daily cross-border) could still mean majority of work time in the US. We need to reconcile work location for state tax and benefits eligibility. For CA withholding we generally base it on where you perform work. If you perform significant work in MX, state withholding might still be CA but we need the record. We'll follow up with a simulated payroll.
border-bot: Automated reminder: employees commuting daily across the US-MX border should consult CBP guidelines and check current wait times. Company cannot provide legal advice on immigration documents.
Mateo (Facilities): For equipment: shipping to MX triggers customs and possibly import duties. We prefer shipping equipment to the US office and marking it as assigned to you there, or you can take company laptop across the border daily. If you request temporary equipment shipped to Tijuana, fill the asset form and Facilities will estimate customs paperwork and insurance. Recipient signature required.
payroll-bot: Action required: Carlos, please choose payroll intent on relocate form (keep US payroll / switch to MX payroll / contractor). Link -> https://payroll.internal/intent-select?req=2461002222
Carlos (Eng): Filled form and checked "keep US payroll" and added schedule details (Mon-Fri in SD morning, afternoons in Tijuana). Requested to ship one extra power adapter to MX (small item).
Nina (People Ops): Got it. We'll route to Payroll + Legal + Facilities. Expect a payroll simulation within 3 business days and a Facilities note on shipping options. If anything changes (e.g., you start doing client work in MX or cross 30 consecutive days there), ping us immediately.
Diego (Legal): We'll review and respond. If Legal needs limitations (e.g., no local contracting, restricted data access from MX), we'll include them in the clearance.
Carlos (Eng): Thanks team  I'll wait for the simulation and ship guidance. Appreciate the quick help. :pray:
